item.title: Note 12
item.description:
Notes No. 12
One trade shows the outcome, not the quality of the decision. A process can only be judged over many trades.
Every trade has two separate qualities: whether the rules were followed, and whether it made money. A trade taken by the rules can lose, because no sound system wins every time, and a trade that breaks the rules can still win by chance. Judging a decision by its result alone is known as outcome bias, and its most costly case is the lucky win, which rewards a mistake and makes it more likely to be repeated. Over a large number of trades, results reflect the process; over a single trade, they mostly reflect chance.
Notes from my trading. Not investment advice.
